standard.title: Measures of turn
standard.description: identify, describe and demonstrate quarter, half, three-quarter and full measures of turn in everyday situations
standard.prior_knowledge: Students give and follow directions using positional and movement language (AC9M1SP02). They have not yet identified fractional turns as measures of rotation or connected turns to the concept of angle.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify, describe and demonstrate quarter, half, three-quarter and full turns in everyday situations, using appropriate language including clockwise and anticlockwise.

nodes.label: Full and half turns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify, describe and demonstrate a full turn and a half turn in everyday contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate a full turn and a half turn with their body or an object; describe each in words.
nodes.typical_width: Identify, describe and demonstrate full and half turns in everyday contexts: spinning, door handles, tap handles, equipment dials; draw labelled diagrams showing direction and amount of turn.
wider: Identify things that turn in the school environment (handles, dials, switches); demonstrate half and full turns for each; label with arrows showing direction
Connect half and full turns to half-past and o'clock on a clock face
success_criteria: Demonstrates a full turn and a half turn correctly with body or object
Describes both turns in words (e.g. 'a half turn faces you the opposite way')

nodes.label: Quarter and three-quarter turns
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify, describe and demonstrate quarter and three-quarter turns, including clockwise and anticlockwise directions.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate a quarter turn clockwise and a quarter turn anticlockwise; identify each correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Identify, describe and demonstrate quarter, half, three-quarter and full turns; use clockwise and anticlockwise language; connect to giving and following directions.
wider: Follow and give movement instructions in a dance or drill: 'quarter turn left, half turn right'; describe the sequence of turns
Program a robot or avatar to navigate a path using quarter, half and three-quarter turns; verify the result

response_modes.reason: Three-quarter turns and the distinction between clockwise and anticlockwise are common error sources. Physical, embodied demonstration across multiple contexts (body, robot, diagrams) helps students build reliable mental models of rotation direction and amount.

success_criteria: Demonstrates a quarter turn correctly in a specified direction (clockwise or anticlockwise)
Identifies a three-quarter turn and distinguishes it from a quarter turn
Uses 'clockwise' and 'anticlockwise' correctly to describe direction of turn

nodes.label: Turns in directions and pathways
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can give and follow instructions involving quarter, half and three-quarter turns to navigate a space or grid.
nodes.minimum_width: Follow a set of instructions involving at least two different turns to reach a target position on a grid.
nodes.typical_width: Give and follow directions involving quarter, half, three-quarter and full turns to navigate grids, floor mazes or robotic pathways; locate an object in a room using fractional turn instructions.
wider: Investigate clock hands: relate quarter-turns to quarter-hours; explain how the minute hand makes a quarter-turn for every 15 minutes
Create a pathway on a grid that requires a partner to use specific turn instructions; verify the pathway works
success_criteria: Follows a set of instructions involving quarter, half and three-quarter turns to reach a target
Gives directions involving fractional turns that another person can follow successfully
